name: Per-tool health view + effectiveness fusion (COMPLEARN/COMPPROOF follow-on)
description: Andrew-direct 2026-07-01 (MSTR CHARTER x2, LD-0239). Assess from real agentOps whether comp-tools are used CONSISTENTLY + CORRECTLY, as a queryable closed learning loop. Andrew verbatim: 'now that we have the comp-tools fairly hammered in, how can we assess from real-life agentOps that they are being used consistently and correctly? Is that being tracked with a mechanism that is easily queryable for an effective learning loop?' Build a fused per-tool HEALTH view over THREE axes -> one verdict + action: USED (compiler-tools-log/tool_activity) x RAIL-CONSISTENT (comp-which-rail.log) x EFFECTIVE (COMPPROOF blind-run REACH x USABILITY, folded in as a RECURRING per-tool probe) -> KEEP / FIX (used+reached-for but doesn't reach the answer -- the highest-value catch, only the EFFECTIVE probe surfaces it) / PROMOTE (effective-but-ignored -> COMPROUTE routing change) / RETIRE (dead). CLOSE the ACCUMULATES-BUT-INERT loop (COMPLEARN D1): make the health view DRIVE the fix/promote/retire decisions, cross-checked by COMPPROOF-D1 autonomy audit that it demonstrably changed behavior. GENUINELY-NEW vs COMPLEARN: (1) the EFFECTIVE axis (COMPPROOF-recurring-probe fusion), (2) the single per-tool 3-axis health query, (3) close-the-loop-as-acceptance-gate. A FUSION + probe-feed + query -- REUSE the shipped substrate (tool_activity catalog + comp_learns_score.py + worklist), do NOT rebuild. PRD docs/architecture/NFRA_TOOLHEALTH_PRD.md.
